summary: Sabbath Camp looks back at the first judges: the generation that forgot, Achsah's bold request, Othniel's Spirit-filled leadership, and Deborah's wise counsel and encouragement.

story_reel.narration: Welcome to Sabbath Camp! This week we entered the Valley of Heroes. Let's remember. After Joshua died, a generation grew up that didn't know God, because no one told them the stories. They fell into a sad cycle: turning away, trouble, crying out, and rescue. But every time they cried out, God sent help. Achsah boldly asked her father for springs of water, and he gave her two. Othniel, filled with God's Spirit, became the first judge. Then God raised up Deborah, who judged Israel under a palm tree and helped people make wise decisions. When Barak was afraid, she said, 'Go! This is the day! Hasn't Yahweh gone out ahead of you?' God sent the rain and the river, and the iron chariots got stuck in the mud. Then Deborah sang a song of victory. This week's big truth: Yahweh can give you wisdom to help others decide well. Being wise doesn't mean being the boss. It means listening to God and pointing others toward Him.

quiz.question: Why did the generation after Joshua forget God?
options: No one told them what God had done
quiz.explanation: Another generation arose who didn't know Yahweh, nor the work which he had done for Israel.

quiz.question: Who was the first judge?
quiz.explanation: Yahweh raised up Othniel, Caleb's younger brother's son, as a savior.

quiz.question: What did Deborah ask Barak on the day of battle?
quiz.explanation: Deborah said, 'Hasn't Yahweh gone out before you?'

micro_prayer.text: Yahweh, thank You for always answering when Your people cry out. Give me wisdom to help others make good choices and to point them to You. Amen.
